ops: Open source collaboration includes a series of open-source related learning materials to help enthusiasts gain basic knowledge of what open source software is, the differences between existing open-source software licenses, how to participate in open source projects, and what a welcoming open source community looks like.
- TP 101: Introduction to open source software
- TP 102: How to use Git and GitHub

- TP 201: Practical Networked Applications in Rust. A series of projects that incrementally develop a single Rust project from the ground up into a high-performance, networked, parallel and asynchronous key/value store. Along the way various real-world Rust development subject matter are explored and discussed.

- TP 202: Distributed Systems in Rust. Adapted from the MIT 6.824 distributed systems coursework, this course focuses on implementing important distributed algorithms, including the Raft consensus algorithm, and the Percolator distributed transaction protocol.
- TP 301: TinySQL, a distributed relational database in Go
- TP 302: TinyKV, a distributed key value database in Go

Sqitch is not tied to any framework, ORM, or platform. Rather, it is a
standalone change management system with no opinions about your database
engine, application framework, or development environment.
Changes are implemented as scripts native to your selected database engine.
Writing a [PostgreSQL] application? Write SQL scripts for [`psql`]. Writing
an [Oracle][orcl]-backed app? Write SQL scripts for [SQL\*Plus].
Database changes may declare dependencies on other changes -- even on
changes from other Sqitch projects. This ensures proper order of
execution, even when you've committed changes to your VCS out-of-order.
Sqitch manages changes and dependencies via a plan file, employing a
[Merkle tree] pattern similar to [Git][gitmerkle] and [Blockchain] to ensure
deployment integrity. As such, there is no need to number your changes,
although you can if you want. Sqitch doesn't much care how you name your
Up until you [tag] and [release] your project, you can modify your change
deployment scripts as often as you like. They're not locked in just because
they've been committed to your VCS. This allows you to take an iterative or
test-driven approach to developing your database schema.

An all-in-one workspace connecting inspiration capture, deep creation, and knowledge compounding (👉 **Explore 19 step-by-step showcases with screenshots**):

|**Writing & Editing**|• Classic 3-pane layout with resizable panel width • Seamless toggle between rich-text WYSIWYG & raw Markdown • Syntax highlighting, math formulas, task lists & Focus Mode • Second-level auto-save, instant multi-device sync & revision history|• **Native Poster Notes**: Canvas-based structured visual card layouts, double-click to edit • **WeChat Official Account Formatter**: One-click copy with inline CSS to newsletters/blogs • **Poster Image Export**: Curated themes, Monogram avatars; export to MD, HTML, or PDF|

|**Organization & Search**|• Infinite-depth notebooks & folder tree navigation • Tagging system, drag-and-drop sorting, batch note merging/moving • Millisecond-level full-text search with historical filtering|• **Standalone Knowledge Base Publishing**: One-click publish entire notebooks as static documentation sites with tree navigation & password protection • Multi-user spaces & physical tenant data isolation|

|**Capture & Media**|• Universal attachment uploads (PDF, Office, audio/video, archives) • Browser extension precision clipping for web text & images • Mobile system share sheet to save photos & articles|• **Deep Multi-Platform Structured Clipping**: Deeply adapted for Xiaohongshu, X (Twitter), Zhihu, Reddit, GitHub, YouTube, Bilibili, and 20+ sources • **WeChat Chat History Archiving**: One-click full transcript import on macOS with timestamps, quotes, emojis, and media • **Client-Side Image Compression**: Automatic 50%–90% silent size reduction; chunked streaming safely supports up to 1 GiB files|

|**Data & Visuals**|• Native table editing & Markdown table rendering • Native Mermaid diagrams (flowcharts, sequence diagrams, architecture)|• **AI Multi-Dimensional Tables**: Prompt-to-database with automatic field typing (tags, dates, selects) • **Public Online Collection Forms**: One-click shareable forms without login, syncing responses into tables in real time • **AI Diagram & Infographic Generation**: In-place creation of timelines, comparison charts, quadrant matrices & mind maps|

|**AI & Ecosystem**|• Companion sidebar AI assistant for summaries, proofreading & translations • BYOK (Bring Your Own Key): compatible with OpenAI, Claude, Gemini & custom endpoints|• **Native Agent Protocols (MCP & ACP)**: Built-in MCP for external agent read/write; ACP in desktop app to drive local agents such as Codex, Claude Code and CodeBuddy directly • **AI RSS Daily Digest**: Automated feed aggregation, AI noise filtering, and structured digest generation • Extensible Plugin Development API|

|**Multi-Device Sync & Foundation**|• Seamless, low-latency sync across desktop, mobile, and web with zero device limits • Official client support across Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android • Offline-first with auto-sync queue: write smoothly offline, automatically resume and sync when reconnected • Standard SQLite database, lossless ZIP backup & Markdown export/import|• **Zero Server Cost for Life**: 100% runnable on Cloudflare Free tier (~150k short notes & ~50k images) • **Flexible Docker Self-Hosting**: One-click deployment for VPS, NAS, or home server with millions of notes & instant sync • Server-side brute-force protection and tenant security|

- **Smooth Migration from Third-Party Apps**: Whether importing via the native one-click GUI (supporting complete notes, hierarchies, and attachments from Evernote, Obsidian, and Joplin) or migrating from Notion, flomo, Memos, and other platforms via AI Agent & MCP, EdgeEver provides seamless, verified data mobility. See the Third-Party Notes Migration Guide.

- **Desktop CloudFlare ImgBed**: The desktop app can also upload inserted images straight to your self-hosted CloudFlare ImgBed with an API token. The upload folder accepts PicList-style placeholders such as `{Y}/{m}/{d}` and `{memoId}`.

Web and desktop apps support functional plugins and custom themes, installable from the official marketplace, GitHub, or a Manifest URL, with seamless sync across your workspace. Developers can extend capabilities using `@edgeever/plugin-api`; see the plugin development guide and marketplace submission policy.

- **Offline-First & Sync Timing**: Web, PWA, and desktop clients automatically upload memo edits after 30 seconds of typing inactivity, and poll for remote changes every 5 minutes while visible; window refocus and manual refresh remain immediate. Configurable via `DEFERRED_MEMO_SYNC_DELAY_MS` and `BACKGROUND_WORKSPACE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` in `apps/web/src/lib/workspace-refresh.ts`.
